research_scope: Five full source-free formulations: strict groupoid-valued presheaf, representable presheaf maps, prime ideal, uniformizer and perfect closure.

amendments.review_rationale: Read a strict groupoid-valued presheaf as an ordinary functor from C-opposite to the category of groupoids, with contravariant pullback functors satisfying literal composition and identity equalities.
amendments.reason: Reviewed complete source formulation and effective previous dependency graph in its own categorical, algebraic and ideal-theoretic context. All earlier classifications preserved.

references.phrase: category Groupoids of groupoids and functors
references.context: Category theory: category Groupoids with small groupoids as objects and ordinary functors as morphisms, with usual functor identities/composition; universe conventions for size apply.
references.reason: The category of groupoids is a separately reusable target of groupoid-valued presheaves and is distinct from a single groupoid.
references.matching_note: Provisional contextual missing identity, source-free and pending global mathematical audit.

references.disposition: The assignment f↦F(f^op):F(U)→F(V) is exactly the action of the strict groupoid-valued presheaf on a base arrow, not a separately assumed fibration pullback construction.
The equalities hold on the nose, not merely up to pseudofunctorial natural isomorphism.

references.phrase: ξ∈G(U) as Yoneda natural transformation h_U→G
references.context: Category theory: the Yoneda correspondence Nat(h_U,G)≅G(U), sending ξ∈G(U) to the natural transformation whose X-component sends f:X→U to G(f)(ξ).
references.reason: Yoneda evaluation correspondence is reusable and cannot be reduced to an arbitrary natural transformation without the representable h_U and variance.

amendments.review_rationale: Read prime ideal of commutative unital ring as proper ideal satisfying ab in P implies a or b in P, distinguishing prime property from maximality.
amendments.reason: Reviewed complete source formulation and effective previous dependency graph in its own categorical, algebraic and ideal-theoretic context. All earlier classifications preserved.

references.context: Commutative algebra: associative commutative ring R with a specified multiplicative identity 1_R; the prime-ideal formulation does not assume the ring is an integral domain.
references.reason: A commutative unital ring is a reusable ambient structure, not the prime ideal itself; compare with the already stored commutative-unital-ring missing candidate.
references.matching_note: Provisional contextual missing identity, source-free and pending global mathematical audit.

references.disposition: The quantified implication ab∈P⇒(a∈P or b∈P), together with P being proper, is exactly the prime-ideal defining axiom.

references.phrase: prime ideal need not be maximal
references.disposition: Maximal ideals are prime for commutative unital rings, but not all prime ideals are maximal.

references.phrase: equality of principal ideal (pi) with m
references.disposition: The equation (π)=m is the defining criterion that π is a uniformizer of the DVR, not a separate mathematical object or assumption that π is a unit.

references.phrase: uniformizer need not be a unit
references.disposition: A uniformizer generates the proper maximal ideal and is not just any invertible element of A.

amendments.review_rationale: Read the perfect closure in positive characteristic inside a fixed algebraic closure, requiring minimal perfect extension and compatible iterated pth-power roots, not arbitrary algebraic elements.
amendments.reason: Reviewed complete source formulation and effective previous dependency graph in its own categorical, algebraic and ideal-theoretic context. All earlier classifications preserved.

references.phrase: compatible iterated p-power roots of elements of k
references.context: Field theory: for each a∈k and n≥1 choose a^{1/p^n} in a fixed algebraic closure of characteristic p, compatibly so (a^{1/p^{n+1}})^p=a^{1/p^n}; these roots generate purely inseparable field extensions.
references.reason: Compatible p-power root towers are reusable algebraic constructions, more specific than a generic root of a polynomial.
references.matching_note: Provisional contextual missing identity, source-free and pending global mathematical audit.

references.disposition: Minimality of the resulting perfect field containing k within a fixed algebraic closure is the defining universal/minimal condition for the perfect closure; a perfect field extension is already linked.
This construction is explicitly restricted to p>0 and does not assert nontrivial perfect closure in characteristic zero.
